title: Fantasy Player News
description: Breaking Fantasy Football player news along with the impact for fantasy managers

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Mike Evans catches three passes in Week 2 win
items.desc: Mike Evans came down with all three of his targets for 54 yards in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
items.impact: Evans gained half of his yards in Sunday's win on one catch, as he was limited overall in volume of targets due to Brock Purdy efficiently spreading the ball around. At this point in his career, Evans is not the top-tier WR he once was, but he is showing immediate rapport with Purdy. Evans has hauled in 9-of-10 targets for 103 yards and a score through two games.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Kyle Juszczyk hits paydirt in Week 2 win
items.desc: Kyle Juszczyk secured both of his targets for 27 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
items.impact: Juszczyk did his thing for the 49ers in Sunday's blowout of the Dolphins. The 10-time Pro Bowl selection scored on a six-yard touchdown strike in the third quarter and gained 21 yards on another catch. He remains a pivotal role player for QB Brock Purdy and the 49ers' offense, but Juszczyk does not get nearly enough touches to make him a fantasy options in the vast majority of leagues.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Kaelon Black gets seven carries in Week 2
items.desc: Kaelon Black gained 25 yards on seven carries in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
items.impact: After gaining 65 yards on 14 carries in Week 1, Black saw his attempts cut in half in Week 2. The 49ers' rushing attack was not very efficient in Sunday's win, but Brock Purdy more than made up for that with his passing prowess. Black has gained 90 yards on 21 carries through two games, and he maintains decent fantasy value as the backup to Christian McCaffrey.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Christian McCaffrey finds the end zone twice in Week 2
items.desc: Christian McCaffrey gained 23 yards on 10 carries and 43 yards on four catches, scoring twice on the ground in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
items.impact: The 49ers' rushing attack was not very efficient in Week 2, but McCaffrey did score a pair of one-yard plunges. As usual, the dual-threat back was also active in the passing game. McCaffrey is up to 29 total touches through two games, averaging 4.6 yards per carry and 7.0 yards per reception. The 49ers appear to be capping the 30-year-old's usage a bit, but he's still a clear RB1, particularly in PPR formats, when healthy.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Brock Purdy turns in tremendous effort against Dolphins
items.desc: Brock Purdy connected on 20-of-22 passes for 287 yards and two touchdowns, adding 30 yards and a touchdown on three carries in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
items.impact: Purdy is off to an outstanding start this season, and he could hardly have been more prolific in Sunday's rout of the Dolphins. The fifth-year QB has completed a ridiculous 80.4% of his passes so far, averaging 246 yards with a 5-1 TD/INT ratio through two games. Purdy has also rushed for 59 yards on eight carries, including a two-yard scoring scramble on Sunday. He'll be a QB to start against the Cardinals in Week 3.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Jets D/ST registers three sacks in Week 2
items.desc: The Jets D/ST registered three sacks while also forcing one turnover (one fumble recovery) in a 20-17 loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 2.
items.impact: The unit was mostly solid outside of a fourth quarter letdown for head coach Aaron Glenn, allowing under 200 offensive yards in a losing effort. The defense will be difficult to trust against a high-powered Detroit Lions offense in Week 3.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Jason Sanders picks up five points in Week 2
items.desc: Jason Sanders converted his lone field goal attempts as well as both of his extra point attempts to finish with five points on the Jets' 20-17 loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 2.
items.impact: Sanders continues a solid start to the season, finishing with five or more points in each of the first two contests. The kicker will look for another steady performance against the Detroit Lions in Week 3.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Packers D/ST picks up four sacks in Week 2 win
items.desc: The Packers D/ST recorded four sacks in a 20-17 win over the New York Jets in Week 2.
items.impact: The unit made stops when it mattered to carry an inconsistent Green Bay offense, allowing 285 offensive yards in the win. The defense will look to take advantage of an underwhelming Atlanta Falcons offense in Week 3.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Eddy Pineiro makes five PATs in Sunday's win
items.desc: Eddy Pineiro did not attempt a field goal but made all five of his PATs in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
items.impact: The 49ers found the end zone with each of their first five drives Sunday afternoon, and did not give Pineiro any field-goal chances. That's obviously not going to be the case each week. The veteran should be a solid fantasy option for a squad that looks really strong so far.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Trey Smack picks up eight points in Week 2
items.desc: Trey Smack converted each of his two field goal attempts as well as both of his extra point attempts to finish with eight points in the Packers' 20-17 win over the New York Jets in Week 2.
items.impact: Smack continues a strong start to the season, racking up eight or more points in each of the first two games. The kicker will look for more success in a favorable Week 3 contest against the Atlanta Falcons.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: 49ers D/ST records four sacks, stifles Dolphins offense
items.desc: The 49ers' defense allowed just 13 points on 284 yards of offense while recording four sacks in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
items.impact: For the second straight week, the 49ers' defense dominated. The unit has surrendered just 20 points in two games, holding both the Rams and Dolphins under 300 yards of total offense. The 49ers will remain a popular play in Week 3 against the Cardinals.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Vikings D/ST disruptive in Week 2
items.desc: The Vikings D/ST registered four sacks while also forcing two turnovers (one interception, one fumble recovery) in a 9-3 win over the Chicago Bears in Week 2.
items.impact: The unit was able to stand tall against a Chicago ground attack, holding both D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai to less than 50 yards rushing each. The defense will look to take advantage of a turnover-prone Tampa Bay Buccaneers offense in Week 3.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Will Reichard perfect in Week 2 win
items.desc: Will Reichard converted all three of his field goal attempts to finish with nine points in a Week 2 9-3 win over the Chicago Bears.
items.impact: Reichard continues a strong start to the season, recording seven or more points in each of the first two games. The kicker will look to provide another solid performance against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 3.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Bears D/ST steady in Week 2 loss
items.desc: The Bears D/ST recorded three sacks in a 9-3 loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 2.
items.impact: The unit made up for a lackluster performance from the offense, allowing just 246 offensive yards in a losing effort. The defense will look for another strong performance against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 3.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Dolphins defense surrenders five touchdowns in Week 2 loss
items.desc: The Dolphins D/ST allowed 35 points on 382 yards of offense in Sunday's blowout loss to the 49ers.
items.impact: The Dolphins' defense had zero answers for the 49ers on Sunday. The Miami unit surrendered a touchdown on each of the 49ers' first five drives, recording no sacks or forcing any turnovers throughout the game. Things won't get much easier for the Dolphins in a Week 3 battle with the Chiefs.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Riley Patterson puts seven points on the board in Week 2
items.desc: Riley Patterson made 2-of-3 field-goal attempts and his only PAT in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the 49ers.
items.impact: Patterson made 2-of-3 field-goal tries for the second consecutive game on Sunday. The 27-year-old kicker actually could be a decent fantasy option, but the Dolphins' offense will be difficult to depend on to provide opportunities.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Greg Dulcich finishes with two receptions in Sunday's loss
items.desc: Greg Dulcich secured 2-of-3 targets for 17 yards in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the 49ers.
items.impact: Dulcich almost replicated his output from Week 1 in this contest. The fifth-year TE has caught 4-of-5 targets for just 35 yards through two games, and he's not been much of a factor in the Dolphins' plodding offense.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Cairo Santos misses field goal in Week 2
items.desc: Cairo Santos converted one of his two field goal attempts in the Bears' 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 2.
items.impact: Santos had a would-be game-tying field goal attempt blocked in the fourth quarter, snapping a 10 kick conversion streak to begin the season. The kicker will look to get back on track against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 3.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Chris Bell a non-factor in Week 2 loss
items.desc: Chris Bell failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the 49ers.
items.impact: Bell gained 25 yards on his only catch in Week 1, but through two games, the rookie has gotten just three total targets from QB Malik Willis. Bell may merit stash status in dynasty formats, but he's off the redraft radar at the moment.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Malik Washington grabs four passes in Week 2 loss
items.desc: Malik Washington secured 4-of-5 targets for 43 yards, adding four yards on one carry in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the 49ers.
items.impact: Washington has now hauled in seven combined passes over the first two weeks for an average of 13.7 yards. His production to this point is likely an indicator of what to expect for the duration of the season in the Dolphins' anemic offensive attack.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Caleb Douglas does little on three targets in Week 2
items.desc: Caleb Douglas caught 2-of-3 targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the 49ers.
items.impact: Douglas had a nice NFL debut, grabbing five passes for 94 yards in Week 1. He came well short of that production against a tougher San Francisco defense in Week 2. Douglas saw 51 snaps for the second straight week, but his output is likely to be volatile all season.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Chargers D/ST plays poorly in loss Sunday
items.desc: The Chargers' D/ST logged two sacks and one interception while allowing 24 points in Sunday's loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
items.impact: Los Angeles' defense has struggled through the first two weeks of the season, despite playing against two teams generally considered among the league's worst. This unit is not worth rostering for a long time with an extremely difficult schedule coming up for the next 7-9 weeks.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Cameron Dicker misses kick in loss Sunday
items.desc: Cameron Dicker went 2-for-2 on his extra-point attempts but missed his lone field-goal attempt in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
items.impact: The Chargers didn't have much going for them on Sunday, including kicking. Dicker misses his lone field-goal against the Raiders, leaving three more points on the field for Los Angeles. Fantasy managers of the 26-year old should consider moving to a different fantasy option for the time being.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Charlie Kolar quiet in loss Sunday
items.desc: Charlie Kolar caught three passes for 21 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
items.impact: Kolar wasn't able to get much going on the stat sheet on Sunday, finishing with just 21 yards on three catches against the Raiders. He may see a bit more work than usual moving forward with David Njoku (knee) quite possibly missing time, but he isn't expected to be a strong fantasy option either way.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Oronde Gadsden II hauls in touchdown Sunday
items.desc: Oronde Gadsden II caught two passes for 18 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
items.impact: Gadsden didn't see a lot of opportunities on Sunday, but he was able to capitalize on one of them by scoring Los Angeles' lone touchdown through the air against the Raiders. He still didn't have a great fantasy total, but he may see an increase in work moving forward with David Njoku (knee) possibly needing to miss time.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Ryan Miller hauls in long touchdown late in Week 2 loss
items.desc: Ryan Miller caught his only target for a 77-yard touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the 49ers.
items.impact: Miller is not a player to suddenly target on the waiver wire. He only played seven snaps Sunday, with his one big play coming when the Dolphins were down 35-6 late in the fourth quarter. The third-year pro was picked up late in the preseason by the Dolphins to add depth at wide receiver.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Tre' Harris leads team in receiving Sunday
items.desc: Tre' Harris caught 1-of-3 targets for 53 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
items.impact: Harris was the leading receiver for the Chargers on Sunday, and he was able to earn that title with just one 53-yard catch on the afternoon. Fantasy managers shouldn't have high hopes for him moving forward after two underwhelming games to start the season.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Keaton Mitchell totals 39 yards Sunday
items.desc: Keaton Mitchell rushed the ball five times for 24 yards and caught one pass for 15 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
items.impact: The veteran running back saw decent involvement on Sunday, totaling 39 yards on his six touches against Las Vegas. He is still squarely behind Omarion Hampton in the pecking order, however, making him irrelevant from a fantasy perspective for the time being.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: De'Von Achane grinds out 93 yards of offense in Week 2
items.desc: De'Von Achane gained 74 yards on 20 carries and caught 3-of-6 targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the 49ers.
items.impact: Achane's touches went up in Week 2, but his efficiency in the Dolphins' anemic offense was about the same. The dual-threat back has yet to find the end zone through two games while averaging just 3.5 yards per carry. He's best viewed as an RB2 for now, with his volume of touches being the main reason. Achane has a tough matchup coming against the Chiefs.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Ladd McConkey underwhelming in loss Sunday
items.desc: Ladd McConkey caught three passes for 35 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
items.impact: McConkey was able to play on Sunday, despite being questionable coming into the week due to an injury he suffered in Week 1. He didn't look very good against the Raiders, however, totaling just 35 yards over the course of the afternoon. He will likely bounce back and return to being a good fantasy option in the near future, but his consistency may be frustrating if Los Angeles' offense continues to struggle.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Quentin Johnston struggles in loss Sunday
items.desc: Quentin Johnston caught 1-of-5 targets for just seven yards and rushed the ball one time for seven yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
items.impact: Los Angeles' offense as a while struggled on Sunday, and Johnston was no exception to that. He wasn't able to haul in all but one of his five targets against the Raiders, and he only ended up contributing 14 total yards over the course of the game. He isn't worth rostering in most league formats at this point in the season.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Malik Willis salvages Week 2 performance with late TD pass
items.desc: Malik Willis completed 14-of-23 passes for 197 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the 49ers.
items.impact: Willis did very little against the 49ers' defense until connecting with WR Ryan Miller on a 77-yard touchdown in the waning stages of Sunday's blowout loss. Unlike in Week 1, Willis did not make up for a lack of passing totals with his running ability. Through two weeks, the Dolphins' offense has largely met the low expectations most had for it. Willis has led the unit to just 13 points in each of the first two games. He'll be toward the bottom of the QB barrel for a Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Omarion Hampton scores once in loss Sunday
items.desc: Omarion Hampton rushed the ball 23 times for 94 yards and a touchdown and caught two passes for 21 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
items.impact: Hampton was one of the lone bright spots for the Chargers on Sunday. He logged 115 total yards and found the end zone once over the course of the afternoon, though he left something to be desired in the passing game. He should continue to be a good fantasy option moving forward, though the present struggles of Los Angeles' offense may cap his upside from a fantasy perspective.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Justin Herbert struggles in loss Sunday
items.desc: Justin Herbert completed 15-of-27 passing attempts for 192 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
items.impact: Herbert didn't look very good on Sunday. He failed to hit 200 total yards and had more interceptions than touchdowns in what turned out to be a two-score loss at the hands of the Raiders, who are frequently regarded as one of the worst teams in the NFL. Los Angeles' offense has been spiraling through the first two weeks of the season, and it's not getting any easier for them with an absolute gauntlet of a schedule coming up over the next 7-9 weeks.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Raiders D/ST stellar in win Sunday
items.desc: The Raiders' D/ST logged three sacks, two interceptions, and a safety while allowing just 14 points in Sunday's win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
items.impact: Las Vegas' defense had a great showing again on Sunday. They allowed Los Angeles' offense to score just 14 points over the course of the game, and they were able to make several big plays to help out their own offense. This unit is not going to be worth rostering for a while, however, as they have quite a difficult schedule coming up over the next handful of weeks.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Matt Gay perfect in win Sunday
items.desc: Matt Gay went 3-for-3 on his extra-point attempts and made his lone field-goal attempt in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
items.impact: The veteran kicker played well on Sunday, making all four of his attempted kicks in a win over the Chargers. He isn't expected to be a good fantasy option for the foreseeable future, however, with a tough schedule coming up for Las Vegas.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Michael Mayer catches three passes Sunday
items.desc: Michael Mayer caught 3-of-4 targets for 23 yards in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
items.impact: Sunday's game brought less involvement for Mayer, as he had half of the receptions that he had in the season opener a week before. He was only able to rack up 23 yards over the course of the afternoon, and now he is set to once again be an irrelevant fantasy option with Brock Bowers (knee) soon to make his return to the lineup.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Cody White hauls in two touchdowns Sunday
items.desc: Cody White caught two passes for 24 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
items.impact: The Raiders were able to score a lot of points on offense on Sunday. White made a couple big plays for them on that front, catching two touchdowns in the team's win over the Chargers. This was a pretty good game for him but he isn't expected to be a fantasy relevant wideout for a while.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Malik Benson held catchless in win Sunday
items.desc: Malik Benson was not able to haul in his lone target in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
items.impact: The rookie was silent on Sunday, failing to catch even a single pass over the course of the afternoon. He remains off of the fantasy radar for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jack Bech totals 25 yards in win Sunday
items.desc: Jack Bech caught two passes for 25 yards in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
items.impact: Bech wasn't able to capitalize on Las Vegas' offensive success on Sunday. He caught just two passes for 25 yards in the team's win over the Chargers, which is quite underwhelming from a fantasy perspective. He isn't expected to be fantasy relevant moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jalen Nailor quiet in win Sunday
items.desc: Jalen Nailor caught 1-of-3 targets for nine yards in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
items.impact: Nailor was a non-factor on Sunday. He caught just one pass against the Chargers and wasn't able to do much of note with it. He isn't expected to be a good fantasy option moving forward, especially with Brock Bowers (knee) set to return to the lineup in the very near future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Tre Tucker stellar in win Sunday
items.desc: Tre Tucker caught 5-of-7 targets for 119 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
items.impact: The Raiders were able to pick up an upset win over the Chargers on Sunday, and Tucker played a big part in that. He led the team in receptions and yards over the course of the afternoon, and he also caught a touchdown, which further helped his fantasy total. He will likely have other big games moving forward, but they will be inconsistent and hard to predict, especially with Brock Bowers (knee) soon to return to the lineup.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Mike Washington Jr. uninvolved in loss Sunday
items.desc: Mike Washington Jr. rushed the ball three times for seven yards and failed to catch his lone target in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
items.impact: Washington saw a decrease in opportunities on Sunday, falling to just three touches after having seven in the season opener a week ago. He isn't a big part of this offense right now and shouldn't be rostered in most league formats for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Ashton Jeanty inefficient in win Sunday
items.desc: Ashton Jeanty rushed the ball 21 times for 48 yards and caught 4-of-7 targets for 15 yards in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
items.impact: Jeanty didn't look great on Sunday. He totaled just 63 on his 28 opportunities against the Chargers, and he wasn't able to get into the end zone at all, which left him with an underwhelming fantasy total. The Raiders have a tough schedule coming up, so the young running back will need to step up his game if he wants to deliver for fantasy managers.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Kirk Cousins tosses three touchdowns in win Sunday
items.desc: Kirk Cousins completed 19-of-29 passing attempts for 253 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
items.impact: Cousins played a good game on Sunday. He threw three touchdowns over the course of the day and he led Las Vegas to a big win over their divisional rivals. He isn't expected to be a good fantasy option himself moving forward but should be good enough to support at least two fantasy options on this offense on a week-to-week basis.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Broncos D/ST holds Jags to 13 points
items.desc: The Broncos D/ST allowed 13 points while notching two sacks and forcing one turnover in a 20-13 win over the Jaguars in Week 2.
items.impact: Denver's defense made life difficult for the Jacksonville offense, holding them to just three points after halftime. It was a needed bounce-back performance after the Broncos struggled on defense against the Chiefs in Week 1. They will look to keep it going in Week 3 against the Rams.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Wil Lutz makes two FGs in Week 2
items.desc: Wil Lutz made both of his field-goal attempts and added two extra points in a 20-13 win over the Jaguars in Week 2.
items.impact: Lutz hit field goals from 20 and 45 yards out in the win. The veteran kicker has made all three of his field goals through the first two games of the season. He will take on the Rams in Week 3.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Evan Engram hauls in 17-yard pass in Week 2
items.desc: Evan Engram caught his lone target for a 17-yard gain in a 20-13 win over the Jaguars in Week 2.
items.impact: Engram was quiet in the comeback win after posting a productive outing back in Week 1. The veteran tight end has now caught five passes for 60 yards and a touchdown through two games. He will be a low-end TE2 in fantasy for Week 3 against the Rams.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Pat Bryant held without a catch in Week 2
items.desc: Pat Bryant was unable to catch his lone target in a 20-13 win over the Jaguars in Week 2. He did add a 16-yard rush in the win.
items.impact: Bryant was shut out just one week after leading the Broncos in receiving. Such is life as a complementary option in a Sean Payton offense. Bryant will be a boom/bust flex option in fantasy heading into Week 3 against the Rams.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Courtland Sutton held to 25 yards in Week 2
items.desc: Courtland Sutton caught three of his four targets for 25 yards in a 20-13 win over the Jaguars in Week 2.
items.impact: Sutton posted a pedestrian stat line in the Broncos' exciting comeback win. It is becoming a concern after he caught just two passes for 11 yards back in Week 1. The Broncos don't seem to be prioritizing getting him the ball as they have in past years, leaving Sutton as a risky flex option in Week 3 against the Rams.
